solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strength shown by prisoner rescued by extraordinary heroes before end of war

indicators.note: something rescued is held safe in another's arms, so the prisoner sits inside the other letters
extraordinary heroes are heroes out of their usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Brave heroes free a prisoner just before a war finishes, displaying great strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' makes HORSEE, 'rescued by' holds POW, and 'end of' gives R. A unit of engine power, not the heroes' might, is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsepower is a unit measuring an engine's power or strength.

clue.text: Start to cut around article on masculine eastern art

indicators.note: around means surrounding the other pieces
to cut a word is to shorten it by its last letter

parts.note: an origin is a start

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions for paper art beginning with a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' trims ORIGIN to ORIGI; 'around' wraps it round AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of paper folding.

clue.text: Nonagenarian, I sense, only partially climbing mountain

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
only partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sensing that a ninety-year-old is managing only part of a mountain climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses IANIS, as a down answer reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the biblical mountain where Moses received the Commandments.

clue.text: Opening that may be on the starboard side, however?

definitions.text: Opening that may be on the starboard side, however?

parts.words: Opening that may be on the starboard side, however?
parts.note: a ship's round window bears the name of the left side of the vessel even when it sits on the right

explanation.walkthrough: Port is a ship's left side and starboard its right, so the joke is that this window keeps its port name wherever it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is the round window in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Predicton a farce, other winds going in a particular direction

indicators.note: going in means entering the other piece

parts.note: west is one particular compass direction

indicators.note: winds as in twists, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone predicts that a farce will unfold, with gusts blowing one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like weather but rearranges A FARCE OTHER into EATHERFORECA, which is 'going in' WEST. 'Predicton' is the clue's misprint of Prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast is a prediction of coming conditions.

clue.text: In boxing arena, I've taken a painful blow for sport!

indicators.note: in places the cry inside the arena

parts.note: boxers fight in a ring
ow is the cry of someone who has just been hurt

explanation.surface: A boxer complains of a painful punch in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing is a sport of racing boats with oars.

clue.text: Fortune in very large inheritance, ultimately

parts.note: fat means bulky, very large

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone's fortune lies in a very large inheritance that eventually comes their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'inheritance', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate and fortune are synonyms for the lot destiny hands out.

clue.text: Spooner's communications device in a warren? That's a sensitive place

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: rabbits, or bunnies, live in a warren
a phone is a communications device

explanation.surface: A rabbit's telephone imagined as a tender spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunny phone becomes a funny bone when the starting sounds swap; the PH sounds like F.
explanation.definitionFit: The funny bone is the elbow nerve that tingles painfully when knocked.

clue.text: Couple with female turning up in book

indicators.note: in places the female inside the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair, with a woman appearing in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes SOW into WOS, which goes into TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, a couple.

clue.text: Scandinavian somewhat off in Norway?

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian feeling a little unwell while visiting Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' points to letters spanning 'off in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native of Finland, a Nordic country often grouped with Scandinavia.

clue.text: Film in right lughole, might you say?

parts.note: split whimsically as lug, slang for an ear, plus hole, a window or opening

explanation.surface: A film playing in someone's right ear, as if heard through headphones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lughole' is British slang for the ear; 'might you say?' flags the playful split into lug (EAR) and hole (WINDOW).
explanation.definitionFit: Rear Window is Alfred Hitchcock's 1954 thriller starring James Stewart.

clue.text: Scandinavian was forced to admit error after volte-face

indicators.note: a volte-face is a complete about-turn, so the assembled letters are read backwards
to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: had, as in 'had to', means was forced
a sin is a wrong, an error

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian made to own up to a mistake after a sudden change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was forced' means 'had (to)'. 'to admit' gives HSINAD, which 'after volte-face' reverses. 'Scandinavian' echoes 9 across's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish describes someone or something from Denmark, a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: Dope after sweetheart, attractive thing

indicators.note: after places the drug word behind the term of endearment

parts.note: honey is an affectionate name for a sweetheart
dope and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Drugs coming after a lover makes something alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeypot is something that draws people in, as honey draws bees.

clue.text: Something sent round

definitions.meaning: a notice distributed to many people at once

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally as one definition, but splits into a mailed notice and a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a printed notice sent widely; the adjective means ring-shaped.

clue.text: Europe, say, on the money, in the money!

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin, money
taken as written
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A cry that Europe is spot on and rich.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is slang for cash; ON TIN goes 'in' CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one example of a continent, a large landmass.

clue.text: Gas bypassing heart in strong animals

indicators.note: bypassing the heart means the middle letters are skipped

parts.note: oxygen is a gas

explanation.surface: Gas skipping the heart of powerful beasts, as if in some medical drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bypassing heart' removes the central YG.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle used as draught animals for their strength.

clue.text: Film the Church time and time again, and the rest

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film
CE is the Church of England
another word for time is era

explanation.surface: A list of films, church, and repeated time, petering out.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is clued twice: T, then ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for and the rest, as in a list.

clue.text: Crew after a word of agreement

indicators.note: after puts the crew behind the a

parts.note: a crew is made up of men

explanation.surface: A crew chasing a word of agreement from the captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said to affirm or agree, as at the end of a prayer.

clue.text: Pole rescuing female, a lifesaver

indicators.note: rescuing means holding the female safe inside

parts.note: a mast is a pole
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A man of Poland saving a woman from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a MAST. A Mae West is an inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mae West is an inflatable life jacket that saves lives at sea.

clue.text: Negotiate honestly in secret

indicators.note: to negotiate a word is to work it round into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice to bargain fairly while keeping things private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' rearranges HONESTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly means doing it covertly.

clue.text: Hide drug in foam

indicators.note: in puts the drug inside the foam

parts.note: lather is soapy foam
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Concealing drugs in foam to smuggle them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but means animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide.

clue.text: Bobby revealed an unsatisfactory alibi?

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a cop
out means exposed, revealed

explanation.surface: A policeman exposes a weak alibi.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop-out is an evasion, a feeble excuse to avoid responsibility.

clue.text: Interval required to reverse X and 1

indicators.note: to reverse something is to turn it back to front

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times
1 is one

explanation.surface: A musical gap needed to undo a multiplication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns TIMES into SEMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest musical interval in Western scales.

clue.text: Heading off, nurse clutching a charm

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed
clutching means holding inside

parts.note: a tender is someone who looks after, a nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse leaving while holding a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' puts A inside TENDER for TENDEAR; 'Heading off' drops the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to win affection, to charm.

clue.text: Unmanned aircraft finished touring Russian capital

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: done means finished

indicators.note: a capital is a first letter

explanation.surface: A drone ending its flight around Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian capital' suggests Moscow, but it is the first letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a remotely piloted aircraft.

clue.text: Again paint crimson and green with speed

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red
eco means environmentally green
rate is a speed

explanation.surface: Instructions to repaint quickly in red and green.
explanation.definitionFit: To redecorate is to paint or paper a room afresh.

clue.text: Central part of tour takes in a hot island

indicators.note: takes in means holds inside
the central part of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The middle of a holiday tour includes a warm island stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central part of' gives OU from tour; 'takes in' puts AH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island where Honolulu lies.

clue.text: Let It Be, Beatles hit, the best by all conclusions

indicators.note: the conclusions of all these words are their final letters

explanation.surface: Praise for Let It Be as the Beatles' finest hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let It Be' looks like the song title but is the definition; 'by all conclusions' takes the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreading instruction meaning let the original text stand.

clue.text: Three-D art, perhaps, last seen in Giza — The Pyramids

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged another way
the last seen of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Three-dimensional art, as at Giza, describing the pyramids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges THREEDART into TETRAHEDR; 'last seen in' adds A from Giza.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramids are solid shapes; a triangular-based pyramid is a tetrahedron, plural tetrahedra.
